title: Is There Ambition in My Heart
description: Is There Ambition in My Heart in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 131, headed “Humility and submission”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Is there am-bi-tion in my heart? Search, gra-cious God, and see; Or do I act a haugh-ty part? Lord, I ap-peal to thee.

lines: Is there ambition in my heart?
Or do I act a haughty part?
I charge my thoughts, be humble still,
Content, my Father, with thy will,
The patient soul, the lowly mind
Let saints in sorrow lie resign'd,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
